Synopsis:
Houthi rebels are seizing Yemen's Red Sea coast, including the strategic port of Mocha, in the most intense fighting since the 2022 ceasefire. The offensive threatens both the Bab al-Mandeb strait and the Strait of Hormuz — two critical chokepoints for global shipping. Iran-backed Houthis are using the campaign to pressure the US into lifting its blockade on Iranian oil tankers. Saudi Arabia is retaliating with airstrikes but faces ground losses. The conflict has already pushed oil above $100/bbl and risks further regional escalation, potentially drawing in Pakistan and Turkey via the Mecca defence agreement.
